thesis: Palantir is compounding revenue at a rate (Q1 2026 +85% y/y, US commercial +133% y/y) that has few precedents at this scale, with raised FY2026 guidance of ~$7.65B revenue and $4.2-4.4B adjusted FCF. The July 2026 rally (+14% for the week) reflects a sovereign-AI partnership with Nvidia, the Army NGC2 award, and rotation back into AI software after a ~27-30% drawdown earlier in 2026. The debate is not growth but price: at roughly $320B market cap and ~145x trailing earnings, the stock embeds continuation of hypergrowth for years.
catalysts: Nvidia sovereign-AI partnership deploying Nemotron models in Palantir platforms for US government and critical infrastructure (announced early July 2026)
US Army selected Palantir Foundry as cloud data layer for NGC2, the Army's highest-priority modernization program (July 2026)
Raised FY2026 guidance: revenue $7.65-7.662B (+71% y/y), US commercial revenue guided +120% y/y (Q1 2026 8-K, May 2026)
DA Davidson upgrade neutral-to-buy, price target $175 (July 2, 2026)
Q2 2026 earnings (early August 2026) - next guidance checkpoint
Michael Burry reduced his publicized short position (late June 2026)
risk_factors: Valuation: ~84x forward GAAP earnings, ~33x forward sales; any growth deceleration is severely punished (stock fell ~27-30% earlier in 2026 on exactly this)
Foundation-model disruption: Anthropic/OpenAI enterprise offerings and hyperscalers (Microsoft, AWS, Databricks) pressure AIP differentiation and pricing power
UK NHS contract (~$440M) at risk of non-renewal after parliamentary committee opposition; expires early 2027
Government revenue concentration and political/procurement cyclicality
Beta 2.10 and retail-heavy shareholder base amplify drawdowns in risk-off tapes

fcf_margin_q1_2026.note: calculated (CFO minus capex over revenue); adjusted 0.57
